summary: Instagram is doing nearly all the work: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 50 views. The best videos make a surprising claim about a sensor or robot ('can't see, only hears/feels', 'robot would fall without it') and are about hands-on maker topics like gyro, clap switch and PIR. Generic 'How does X work?' videos on everyday places (lift, mall door, tap, smoke detector) get far less, and the one English video got no Instagram reach at all.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first. Subject is a small maker-relevant sensor or robot behaviour (gyro, clap switch, PIR, IR, mic, line follower). Hook is a surprising claim or 'it doesn't do what you think' ('Nahi... sirf...', 'Ke bina turant gir jaata'), with a short punchy Hinglish title and one emoji. Clap switch, gyro and PIR also earn the best likes, saves and YouTube views, and the IR robot-wall video earned the most shares.
doMore: Lead with a myth-busting or 'without this it fails' hook in the first line on screen
Cover Arduino-module and robot topics (gyro, IR, PIR, mic, line follower) rather than public-place gadgets
Make follow-ups to the winners, such as a clap switch part 3, PIR vs IR, and gyro in drones
Post Instagram-first and ask viewers to save the video, since saves and shares show real interest
Test YouTube separately with a stronger title and a hook in the first 2 seconds, since it barely moves now
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise pata chalta hai? 🤔' titles on lifts, mall doors and taps
Near-duplicate topics (smoke detector x2, IR dark x2, tap x2) posted within days of each other
English narration until Hindi YouTube is fixed, since the single English test got no Instagram reach
